BiblicalUsage: Ahisamach is named three times, always as the father of Oholiab, the craftsman God filled with wisdom to work the tabernacle — his son's hands built God's house, and his father is remembered for it.
TheologicalSignificance: There is no teaching in the father's name alone. But I believe the passage around it teaches plenty: God gives skill, not just zeal, for the work of His house — and He names the workmen.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
